Gadd45 regulates fate decisions of myeloid-type blood cells in Drosophila
summary: Growth arrest and DNA damage-inducible 45 (Gadd45) is a conserved, stress-responsive regulator linking cellular stress and cytokine signaling to cell-cycle control, DNA repair, apoptosis, and differentiation. Altered Gadd45 expression has been associated with mammalian solid tumors and hematopoietic malignancies. Gadd45 also supports cytokine-induced myeloid differentiation, though the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Using the Drosophila hematopoietic system and in vivo genetic and cell-biological approaches, we investigated Gadd45's role in myeloid-type blood cell development. We show that Gadd45 selectively regulates crystal cells by reducing their differentiation and impairing maintenance, while leaving plasmatocyte differentiation unchanged. However, Gadd45 overexpression promotes lamellocyte differentiation, a response typically observed during larval immune challenges and injury. Mechanistically, Gadd45 overexpression induces lamellocyte differentiation through Toll, JNK, and JAK/STAT signaling. Furthermore, Gadd45 overexpression does not induce cell death but alters cell-cycle status in the lymph gland. Our study provides new insight into Gadd45's specific role in crystal cell development and lamellocyte-associated differentiation in Drosophila.

title: Convergent Genomic Signatures of Selection in Thar: Genetic trade-offs for desert survival
summary: Background: Desert environments provide a setting for natural biological experiments to cope up with simultaneous stressors of extreme temperatures, aridity, UV exposure, and limited food resources. Biological adaptations that support living in such an environment could become liabilities when the environment and lifestyle change due to gene-environment mismatch. We explored whether genetically and culturally diverse endogamous native populations of the Thar exhibit convergent signatures of selection to desert conditions and whether the selected loci have implications in traits and disease susceptibilities relevant to non-native transitions. Results: We report 348 high-confidence variants across 45 candidate genes from a study on 176 individuals from eight genetically distinct Thar populations. These genes identified from humans and other desert inhabitants display convergent evolution with multiple selection scans (PBSn1, Tajima`s D, iHS, and XPEHH) in diverse Thar populations. Prominent genes include ZNF385D, SGCZ, SARDH, SLC12A3, etc. Selected variants essential in the desert environment were associated with complex traits like lipid metabolism, hypertension, renal and cardiovascular diseases, and addiction in GWAS and PheWAS. Noteworthy, in a syntenic locus, eQTLs in SARDH, which modulates DBH implicated in addiction, suggest a potential link with survival advantage in an uncertain desert environment. Likewise, a selected variant (rs7204044) in SLC12A3, implicated in hypertension in non-desert populations, seems to be a key to water-salt homeostasis in desert natives. Conclusions: These findings suggest that variants linked to adaptive traits in desert conditions could be linked to maladaptation in an altered environment. This has potential health consequences in climatic and lifestyle transitions among native inhabitants.

title: A hydrogenase-like activity associated with mitochondrial Complex I under hypoxia in vascular plants
summary: Abstract Molecular hydrogen (H2) evolution by higher plants under oxygen limitation was reported more than six decades ago, yet its origin, biochemical basis and physiological significance remain unresolved. Here, we localize this activity to a mitochondrial, Complex I-associated electron-transfer system: fractions from etiolated Vigna radiata hypocotyls accumulated H2 under hypoxia at mildly acidic pH. H2 accumulation was nearly abolished by rotenone and sensitive to perturbations of Complex II, quinone-pool turnover, terminal oxidases and protonmotive force. NADH-generating substrates and succinate-fumarate stimulated H2 accumulation, while metabolic profiling linked H2 production to succinate and NADH accumulation. Cumulative H2 production exceeded the measured NADH pool by approximately two orders of magnitude, requiring sustained NADH regeneration. Our data support a model in which mature Complex I and CI*, a Complex I assembly or remodeling state, have distinct roles. TCA-cycle dehydrogenation and potentially succinate-driven reverse electron transfer (RET) through mature Complex I replenish the matrix NADH pool, whereas CI* may consume NADH through an H2-evolving branch, regenerating NAD. This model identifies a conditional redox function for CI* and an electron outlet coupled to continuous NADH cycling. Diversion of reducing equivalents into H2 could attenuate the corresponding ROS signature, helping explain the elusive physiological evidence for plant RET. Structural and computational analyses support flavin-based electron bifurcation across the FMN-Fe-S branch, although the catalytic steps remain unverified. Together, these findings suggest that Complex I assembly states may reshape electron fate under hypoxia, exposing latent hydrogenase-related chemistry linked to Complex I's evolutionary ancestry. Keywords: molecular hydrogen, mitochondria, Complex I assembly intermediate, electron bifurcation, hypoxia, alternative oxidase, reverse electron transport, flavin, plant metabolism

title: The compartmentalized activity of a legume subtilase SBT12a allows symbiosome stabilization
summary: The stabilization of rhizobia in specialized organelles, called symbiosomes, is an evolutionary hallmark for maintaining high rates of nitrogen fixation in legumes. This is achieved by releasing thousands of bacteria from nodular infection threads into a single plant cell, which poses a great challenge for the host to keep control over these differentiated bacteria. Considering the importance of proteolytic degradation of antimicrobial proteins or generation of symbiosis-promoting signalling factors, proteolytic activity may represent a key regulatory system in this process. Here, we identified the Medicago truncatula subtilisin-like serine protease (subtilase, SBT) 12a acting as a novel regulator of symbiosome functionality and maintenance. Loss-of-function mutations in SBT12a led to severe symbiotic defects with nodules of sbt12a being characterized by high level induction of defense/senescence-related genes. Using untargeted proteomic High-efficiency Undecanal-based N-Termini EnRichment (HUNTER), we identified candidate substrates of SBT12a and individually confirmed intrinsic cleavage sites. Our analysis revealed that SBT12a activity within symbiosomes is associated with the proteolytic regulation of DNF2, a symbiotic protein that is specifically required to prevent defense response and premature nodule senescence during nitrogen fixation. Together, our findings position SBT12a as a central host factor controlling symbiosome performance.

title: A functional analysis of action potential generation in the axon initial segment in two autism mouse models with loss-of-function mutations of the Nav1.2 sodium channel
summary: Loss-of-function (LoF) mutations of the SCN2A gene, coding for Nav1.2 Na+ channels, are among the leading genetic contributors to autism spectrum disorders and intellectual disability (ASD/ID). The haploinsufficient Scn2a knock-out mouse (Scn2a+/-), displaying ASD/ID-like phenotypes, is commonly used as model for this channelopathy, although this specific mutation has not been identified in patients. We investigated the action potential (AP) generation in the axon initial segment (AIS) of layer-5 neocortical pyramidal neurons in wild-type (Scn2a+/+) mice, in Scn2a+/- mice and in mice carrying the missense mutation L1314P (Scn2a+/L1314P), identified in an ASD/ID patient. We recorded somatic action potentials (APs), and imaged Na+, Ca2+ and APs in the AIS, in females during postnatal (P) P21-40. During maturation from P21-24 to P30-40: (1) the ratio between Na+ influx in proximal and distal AIS sites (Rp/d) increased; (2) the delay between distal and proximal Ca2+ currents increased; (3) the half-width of the AP (APwid) in the soma decreased. We revealed that this maturation process is different in both Scn2a+/- and Scn2a+/L1314P mice, but in divergent manner. With respect to Scn2a+/+, Scn2a+/- cells were characterised by smaller Rp/d and delay values at P30-40, and wider somatic APwid at P21-24, whereas Scn2a+/L1314P cells by shorter AIS APwid at P21-24. Using a biophysical model, mimicking maturation changes in terms of Nav1.2, of a K+ channel and of voltage-gated Ca2+ channels, we reproduced the ensemble of experimental results, establishing that Scn2a+/- cells exhibit a combination of Nav1.2 LoF and delayed development, whereas Scn2a+/L1314P cells are characterised by AIS disruption involving strongly increased functional K+ channels. We conclude that diverse Nav1.2 LoF cases lead to different developmental paths involving other channels.

title: Developmental timeline of the lateral olfactory tract innervation of piriform cortex
summary: The development of the lateral olfactory tract (LOT) begins embryonically and is closely linked to the differentiation of olfactory bulb (OB) projection neurons, mitral and tufted cells, whose axons form the LOT. Here, we implemented calretinin (CR) as a proxy to characterize LOT development. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) for CR revealed expression in most mitral/tufted cells, with lower levels in the dorsal OB. This mirrored a reduced CR labeling in a restricted ventral LOT domain, suggesting topographic organization of OB projections. To achieve axonal resolution, we used Calb2-CreERT2 x Ai14 mice to label CR+ neurons and their axons with tdTomato. Expression began at E12, when pioneer LOT axons reach the anterior piriform cortex (APC) and posterior brain regions. From E13-E14, axon density increased, contributing to LOT thickening and extension toward the amygdala. Axonal arborization was not evident in the posterior piriform cortex (PPC) until E15. Electron microscopy revealed excitatory asymmetric and inhibitory symmetric synapses in the APC as early as E13, with relatively stable embryonic densities. Postnatally, excitatory synapses increased in both APC and PPC between P9 and P21. Collectively, this work establishes a developmental timeline of LOT formation and sheds light on fundamental aspects of the assembly of olfactory cortical circuits.

title: Separating robust from fragile cell-type changes in spatial transcriptomics using screening label uncertainty to identify composition effects
summary: Imaging-based spatial transcriptomics platforms such as 10x Xenium measure thousands of genes in intact tissue at single-cell resolution, making them attractive for screening which cell populations change between experimental conditions. In small studies, however, apparent changes in cell-type composition can arise from misannotated cells rather than biology, and the reliability of individual cell-type calls is rarely reported. We present SLUICE (Screening Label Uncertainty to Identify Composition Effects), an R/Seurat workflow that classifies each cell by atlas-informed marker scoring and records a per-cell confidence margin and runner-up identity. Each group difference is then tested against three diagnostics: region-specific confidence thresholds, sensitivity analyses that reassign borderline calls, and single-gene driver checks that combine gene co-detection, runner-up identity, and spatial location. Applied to Xenium Prime 5K data from six mice (three traumatic brain injury, three sham) in two contrasting regions, the hippocampus and the optic tract, confidence thresholds differed almost sevenfold between regions (0.17 vs 0.026), showing that a fixed cutoff does not transfer between tissues. Driver checks identified mislabelled populations that margin-based filtering left in place, including Klotho (Kl)-expressing neurons called choroid plexus in the hippocampus and Csf3r-expressing myeloid cells called neutrophils in the optic tract. Excluding the neutrophil panel reduced the number of optic tract categories whose group difference changed direction from five to two (one of which was the Unclassified category), while the major glial populations were stable across all analyses. SLUICE separates robust from fragile composition changes, identifying which shifts merit experimental follow-up before time and tissue are committed to them. Code is available at https://github.com/rebeccasakko/hippocampus-xenium-analysis.
